title: Review of c02's FCH chemoton (SIBE): on fresh seed 21 bilayer bodies form from noise and persist (S, I), but catalyst-free rings persist as well as catalyst-carrying ones, the radial catalyst layer is weak (rim/core 1.2), and starved bodies shrink without dying by t=600
summary: Looked at channels_seed0_seed1.png and starve_fork.png first, then read world.py: K is autocatalytic everywhere (a K^2 P) and held on bilayers by the exp(-beta(u+1)) min-face gate; amphiphile is made by K from the fed precursor and decays everywhere. Re-ran the claimed world in labkit on seed 21 (rerun/) and its feed-cut fork (world_starve.py, feed off at t=300, starve/; identical to the rerun until t=300). From an unstructured noisy bath, bilayer bodies form by t~50: one three-armed bilayer that carries the catalyst (pink on the arms, with a dark precursor-depleted halo) and several catalyst-free rings and rods; all persist to t=600 at bounded size (labkit: 5 persistent tracks, final 5 components). labkit's radial catalyst profile over 29 individuals: rim/core 1.2, rim/outside 2.22, 5/29 membrane-like; amphiphile rim/core 1.01. In the fork the catalyst-carrying body shrinks to a small three-lobed cluster and the rings shrink to micelle clusters, but every body is still present at t=600, while in the fed run the bodies keep their size.

observations.S: rerun/sheet.png t=0: noise over the whole domain; bodies by t~50
observations.I: rerun/sheet.png and FACTS.md: 5 persistent bilayer bodies (rings, a rod and a three-armed catalyst-carrying body) to t=600

seeds_run.result: partial: bodies form and persist; catalyst layer weak in labkit; starved bodies shrink but do not die by t=600

controls_run.E: starve/ (feed cut at t=300, same seed; fed twin = rerun/)

verdicts.limitation: B: the catalyst does sit on the bilayer of the one catalyst-carrying body (visible on its arms), but labkit's aggregate radial score is rim/core 1.2 with 5/29 individuals membrane-like, below the 1.5 gate; the body is a thin bilayer, so a 'rim' and 'core' of the catalyst are hard to separate and I could not confirm a layer distinct from interior and exterior. E: the RUBRIC L4c fork must show individuals die; on seed 21 the starved bodies shrink (to micelle clusters) but none is gone by t=600, and catalyst-free rings persist in the fed run beside the catalyst-carrying body, so body survival does not visibly depend on carrying the catalyst (consistent with the established finding that the amphiphile is one shared pool). The same individuals do not show S, I, B and E together: the persistent rings carry no catalyst. One fresh seed.
